sentences.zh: 但就紧身胸衣的这种衰落与法国大革命的巧合而言，

sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，不是吗，通过抛弃束胸，你在法国，当然是在拥抱一种政治自由主义，一种政治自由。

sentences.en: I mean, would that be too excessive to say that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这样说会不会太夸张了？

sentences.zh: 如果确实如此，那么为什么这种情况也在英国发生呢？

sentences.zh: 因为据推测，

sentences.zh: 法国和英国时尚之间的关系，以及谁影响了谁，是复杂且多层次的。

sentences.en: And yes, certainly in France, kind of conceptually, that casting off of previous shackles.

sentences.en: I mean, as I say, this has been building in art and court circles throughout the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我所说，这在整个
1780年代的艺术和宫廷圈子中一直在酝酿。

sentences.en: So, the French Revolution kind of crystallizes this manifestation.

sentences.en: But in Britain as well, I think there's that sense of liberty and democracy, because for many in France, the British

sentences.en: So, there is, I mean, there are also the sort of the general tides of fashion.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，也有那种普遍的时尚潮流。

sentences.zh: 当事情发生时，人们会拥抱它们。

sentences.en: But there's a new naturalism that is also supposedly very commensurate with the British character, that the British are easy, they are natural, they are simple, they're not
sentences.zh: 但有一种新的自然主义，据说也非常符合英国人的性格，英国人是随性的，他们是自然的，他们是简单的，他们不像法国人那样

sentences.en: affected and fussy, like the French, obviously.
sentences.zh: 矫揉造作和挑剔，显然。

sentences.zh: 所以，这其中带有一点浪漫主义色彩，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 即某种从理性与秩序向更自由方向的转变。

sentences.en: Is that, am I over-egging that?
sentences.zh: 这是……我是不是有点夸大其词了？

sentences.en: Or is that-
sentences.zh: 还是说——

sentences.en: No, I think that's a very valid point.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这是一个非常中肯的观点。

sentences.en: And for all that the adoption of kind of classical influence in dress is supposedly, you know, looking into that kind of clean, pure, philosophical, ancient world,
sentences.zh: 尽管在服饰中采用古典风格据说是为了探寻那种纯净、哲学、古老的世界，

sentences.en: it is absolutely a romanticism.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是一种浪漫主义。

sentences.en: And the 1790s is also the period where in continental philosophy, the, you know, romantic philosophy is building.
sentences.zh: 18世纪90年代也是欧洲大陆哲学中浪漫主义哲学兴起的时期。

sentences.en: So, there's, it's looking back at the past and kind of, you know, using it as an influence for what's slightly costumey in fashion.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种回望过去，并将其作为时尚中略带戏服感元素的影响。

sentences.en: So, an emblematic example of that would be Emma Hamilton, would it?
sentences.zh: 那么，艾玛·汉密尔顿（Emma Hamilton）就是一个典型的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, tell us about Emma Hamilton, who marries the ambassador, the British ambassador to Naples,
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲艾玛·汉密尔顿吧，她嫁给了英国驻那不勒斯大使，

sentences.en: but is most famous for having a relationship with Admiral Nelson, but who is kind of a celebrity, isn't she, for her kind of attitudinizing in wispy classical dress, but is a very,
sentences.zh: 但她最出名的是与纳尔逊海军上将的关系，而且她本人也是一位名人，不是吗？因为她穿着轻薄的古典服饰摆出各种姿态，而且她是一个非常、

sentences.en: very romantic figure in every sense of the word.
sentences.zh: 非常有浪漫色彩的人物，名副其实。

sentences.en: She absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 她确实是。

sentences.en: And one of the things that, you know, people of good standing and connections did when they went to Naples was to go and see Emma Hamilton's attitudes.
sentences.zh: 当时，有身份、有门路的人去那不勒斯时，都会去观看艾玛·汉密尔顿的“姿态表演”。

sentences.en: And she would kind of do these tableaus where just using basically drapery and, and scarves.
sentences.zh: 她会利用简单的帷幔和围巾来表演这些静态画面。

sentences.en: And again, in that very simple tradition, she would kind of take attitudes and form like still lives that were inspired by
sentences.zh: 同样，遵循那种非常简约的传统，她会摆出各种姿态，形成如同静物画般的造型，灵感来源于

sentences.en: the classical world and much by the sort of antiquarian objects that her husband collected.
sentences.zh: 古典世界，以及她丈夫收藏的许多古董物件。

sentences.en: And there was people who saw it kind of had trouble describing the, the particular quality of it,
sentences.zh: 当时观看的人很难描述那种独特的质感，

sentences.en: but it seemed to sort of, it was magical almoSt. She seemed to kind of step out of the past and she
sentences.zh: 但它似乎有一种魔力。她仿佛是从过去走出来的人，而且她

sentences.en: was doing so with all of her magnificent chestnut hair unbound to the knees, you know, just wrapped in, in very simple clothing.
sentences.zh: 表演时，那一头华丽的栗色长发垂至膝盖，身上只裹着非常简单的衣物。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of evidence to suggest that her fame and beauty and popularity was also very influential on travelers then returning home from Britain,
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明，她的名气、美貌和受欢迎程度对当时从英国返乡的旅行者影响很大，

sentences.en: people like Lady Charlotte Campbell, who then started kind of imitating, not so much classical dress, but Emma Hamilton's version of classical dress.
sentences.zh: 比如夏洛特·坎贝尔夫人（Lady Charlotte Campbell），她开始模仿的与其说是古典服饰，不如说是艾玛·汉密尔顿版本的古典服饰。

sentences.en: So that raises the interesting question about fashion more generally, which is,
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个关于时尚的更有趣的问题，那就是：

sentences.en: this is an age where fashion, the idea of fashion exists, the word fashion?
sentences.zh: 这是一个存在时尚的时代吗？“时尚”这个词本身存在吗？

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 非常存在。

sentences.en: And how much does that depend on, first of all, how much does that depend on individual trendsetters?
sentences.zh: 那么，这在多大程度上取决于个人潮流引领者呢？

sentences.en: So, you know, Emma Hamilton is the classic example, I suppose, or Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 我想，艾玛·汉密尔顿或玛丽·安托瓦内特（Marie Antoinette）就是典型的例子。

sentences.en: And secondly, how is that disseminated?
sentences.zh: 其次，它是如何传播的？

sentences.en: So is it all through print culture?
sentences.zh: 是通过印刷文化吗？

sentences.en: Is it through pamphlets and, well, I guess newspapers?
sentences.zh: 是通过小册子，还是报纸？

sentences.en: I mean, how does it, how does it, yeah, how does it travel?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它是如何传播的？

sentences.en: For me, this has been one of the most interesting things in really researching the Regency period and trying to determine how fashion does travel.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是研究摄政时期并试图确定时尚如何传播时最有趣的事情之一。

sentences.en: And as far as I can tell, it's really through people.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它确实是通过人来传播的。

sentences.en: The influence of visual print media is not nearly as strong as we think it is at the time.
sentences.zh: 视觉印刷媒体的影响力远没有我们想象的那么大。

sentences.en: We are left with, you know, thousands of Regency fashion plates, but that's kind of not how people were really getting their influence.
sentences.zh: 我们留下了成千上万的摄政时期时尚版画，但这并不是人们真正获取时尚影响的方式。

sentences.en: We also have to remember that British society is much smaller at the time.
sentences.zh: 我们还要记住，当时的英国社会规模要小得多。

sentences.en: So if you're in London, it's very likely you could see Lady Charlotte Campbell on the street or in Hyde Park.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在伦敦，你很有可能在街上或海德公园看到夏洛特·坎贝尔夫人。

sentences.en: You can actually go and watch the fashion makers, the tastemakers in London.
sentences.zh: 你可以亲自去观察伦敦的时尚制造者和品味引领者。

sentences.en: And then if you're going to your milliner, your dressmaker, they're going to tell you what other people are buying.
sentences.zh: 当你去女帽商或裁缝店时，他们会告诉你别人在买什么。

sentences.en: And even if you're further out into the country, your cousin, your friend who's in London can say, I saw a lady so-and-so wearing such and such, or, you know,
sentences.zh: 即使你住在偏远的乡村，你在伦敦的表亲或朋友也会告诉你，我看到某某夫人穿了什么，或者，你知道，

sentences.en: I noticed that these veils or this kind of thing is in fashion, which Jane Austen does a lot in her letters.
sentences.zh: 我注意到这些面纱或这类东西很流行，简·奥斯汀在她的信件中就经常提到这一点。

sentences.en: So there's a sense of kind of people transmitting through their own experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们通过自己的亲身经历来传播时尚。

sentences.en: And then also people watching what other people are wearing and taking that on board.
sentences.zh: 人们也会观察别人的穿着并加以采纳。

sentences.en: And I think that that's actually still the strongest transmitter of fashion in this period.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上仍然是这一时期时尚传播最强有力的途径。

sentences.en: But presumably for that to work, you need a certain degree of infrastructure for people to see a fashionable woman, what she's wearing, and then to have it copied.
sentences.zh: 但要让这种方式奏效，大概需要一定的基础设施，让人们能看到时尚女性的穿着，然后进行仿制。

sentences.en: So you'd need the shops, you'd need the milliners, you'd need the fabrics, you'd need the industrial infrastructure that would be capable of doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要商店、女帽商、布料，以及能够实现这一点的工业基础设施。

sentences.en: And this is the age when Napoleon famously dismisses the British as a nation of shopkeepers.
sentences.zh: 这正是拿破仑那句名言的时代，他嘲讽英国是一个“店主之国”。

sentences.en: Is the fact that you have this infrastructure, is that, do you think, how important a role is that playing in kind of expediting this creation of a fashion industry?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种基础设施在加速时尚产业形成的过程中扮演了多重要的角色？

sentences.en: It's absolutely huge.
sentences.zh: 非常巨大。

sentences.en: You know, at this sort of period in the late 18th century, along the Strand and along Oxford Street, it's basically four miles of shops.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪末的这段时期，沿着河岸街（The Strand）和牛津街，基本上有四英里长的商店。

sentences.en: And then, you know, further into sort of the more fashionable areas in Mayfair and along Bond Street.
sentences.zh: 然后，在梅菲尔区和邦德街等更时尚的区域，情况也是如此。

sentences.en: So London is absolutely full of retailers and wholesalers and warehouses.
sentences.zh: 所以伦敦到处都是零售商、批发商和仓库。

sentences.en: And not only are people going to London to shop, as in Pride and Prejudice, when Mrs. Bennett is panicking, because Lydia won't know the best warehouses to go to in London.
sentences.zh: 人们不仅像《傲慢与偏见》里那样去伦敦购物——班内特太太当时很慌张，因为莉迪亚不知道伦敦最好的仓库在哪里——

sentences.en: Smaller retailers outside the capital are also buying from
sentences.zh: 首都以外的小型零售商也从伦敦进货，

sentences.en: London, they will go up to town and then bring their stock in and also see what people are wearing and doing there.
sentences.zh: 他们会去城里进货，顺便看看那里的人在穿什么、做什么。

sentences.en: So there is a robust network of transmission.
sentences.zh: 所以存在一个强大的传播网络。

sentences.en: And you could also do it by mail.
sentences.zh: 你也可以通过邮寄来完成。

sentences.en: So people would send you fabric samples.
sentences.zh: 人们会给你寄布料样本。

sentences.en: There was a lot of proxy shopping where if a friend of yours is going to a major urban centre, it could be London or Bath, but even, you know, Manchester, Birmingham,
sentences.zh: 当时有很多代购，如果你的朋友要去大城市，可能是伦敦或巴斯，甚至曼彻斯特、伯明翰、

sentences.zh: 爱丁堡，他们会代你购物。

sentences.en: And you say, you know, please get me the most fashionable muslin, or I want a very nice yellow cane brick.
sentences.zh: 你会说，请帮我买最时髦的细棉布，或者我想要一种非常漂亮的黄色帆布。

sentences.en: And then they will go and see what other people are wearing and kind of get the intelligence and come back and go, this is what, this is what, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后他们会去看看别人在穿什么，打听情报，回来后告诉你，这是什么，这是什么，你知道，

sentences.en: looked nice, or this is what I could get, or this is what they say is the most appropriate.
sentences.zh: 看起来不错，或者这是我能买到的，或者这是他们说最合适的。

sentences.en: So it really is relying on networks of acquaintance, and that social infrastructure that so holds up
sentences.zh: 所以它确实依赖于熟人网络，以及那种支撑着中产阶级及以上阶层的社会基础设施，

sentences.en: the middle classes and above and that, you know, Austen's novels, in a sense, really demonstrate how those connections and acquaintance work.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀的小说在某种意义上确实展示了这些联系和熟人关系是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And fashion is running exactly along those lines as well.
sentences.zh: 时尚也正是沿着这些路线传播的。

sentences.zh: 那么，在那些被认为最时尚的大都市之外，传播速度如何呢？

sentences.en: So in other words, if you think about a different era, like, you know, the joke that's always made about the 1960s, say, is that everybody is wearing a miniskirt
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你想到另一个时代，比如关于20世纪60年代的那个笑话，大家都说每个人都在卡纳比街穿迷你裙，

sentences.en: in Carnaby Street, but in Hull, people aren't wearing miniskirts until 2012.
sentences.zh: 但在赫尔（Hull），人们直到2012年才穿上迷你裙。

sentences.en: How soon are people in Hull wearing the new fashions that are inspired by the sort of the Emma Hamiltons of this world?
sentences.zh: 赫尔的人们多久才能穿上受艾玛·汉密尔顿这类人启发的时尚新装？

sentences.en: Basically, as soon as information and income will allow them to.
sentences.zh: 基本上，只要信息和收入允许，他们就会穿。

sentences.en: So if you've got the wherewithal, and you're, you know, waiting eagerly for news from London about what the latest fashions are,

sentences.en: and you go into your local shop and go, all right, I'm going to buy a muzzle and try and imitate this, you can do it kind of fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 你走进当地商店说，好吧，我要买块细棉布试着模仿一下，你很快就能做到。

sentences.en: There is a school of thought that says that when, because, you know, one of the reasons I also like the Regency period is Australia has a history,
sentences.zh: 有一种学派认为，因为——你知道，我喜欢摄政时期的另一个原因是澳大利亚有历史，

sentences.zh: 此时已有白人殖民历史。

sentences.en: But the settlers in England who, in Britain, in Australia, who had a six month wait for goods from Britain, actually, that wasn't much longer than, you know,

sentences.en: if you're in sort of the Welsh hills, or maybe the Scottish Highlands.
sentences.zh: 或者苏格兰高地等待的时间长多少。

sentences.en: So it's, it could be relatively faSt. And in fact, there's a wonderful quote from the Irish author, Mariah Edgeworth, who says that,
sentences.zh: 所以它可能相对较快。事实上，爱尔兰作家玛丽亚·埃奇沃思（Maria Edgeworth）有一句精彩的话，她说，

sentences.en: you know, with the post and the roads that we have now, it's almost like everyone can know what everyone's doing at the same time.
sentences.zh: 有了现在的邮政和道路，几乎每个人都能同时知道别人在做什么。

sentences.en: And it's like magical fairies, which, you know, in our day and age seems very slow.
sentences.zh: 就像魔法仙子一样，这在我们这个时代看来似乎很慢。

sentences.en: But she was impressed by how soon people could know what was happening and what was in fashion.
sentences.zh: 但她对人们能如此迅速地获知正在发生的事情和流行趋势感到印象深刻。

sentences.en: Dominic compared this to the 60s, where the sense of a kind of generational divide and is very strong.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克将此与60年代进行了比较，当时代际鸿沟感非常强烈。

sentences.en: And also the kind of the pleasure that the fashionable take in shocking
sentences.zh: 还有时尚人士以震惊那些对穿着有老派观念的人为乐。

sentences.en: people with more old fashioned takes on what you should be wearing.
sentences.zh: 我印象非常深刻，你引用了一本杂志，描述了震惊的老太太和冷哼的老绅士，

sentences.en: And I was really straight, you quote, you quote a magazine that describes shocked old ladies and snorting old gentlemen,
sentences.zh: 哀叹现代潮流，完全缺乏尊重，当今女孩行为大胆，尤其是她服装的极端不雅。

sentences.en: bewailing modern tendencies, the total lack of respect, the boldness of behaviour of the girl of today, and in particular, the extreme indelicacy of her clothing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这简直可以用来描述60年代，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that could be describing, I mean, that could be describing the 60s, couldn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, and really, really strikes.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上所有的时尚革命，比如60年代、朋克，所有我们熟悉的现代英国的东西，

sentences.en: So is, again, is basically all the kind of revolutions of fashion, so the 60s, punk, everything, all the kind of stuff that we're familiar with in modern Britain.
sentences.zh: 你认为，认为摄政时期发生了类似的事情是时代错误吗？

sentences.en: Do you think it does it, is it anachronistic to think of something similar to that happening in the Regency?
sentences.zh: 但摄政时期是第一次伟大的时尚革命。

sentences.en: But the Regency is the first great fashion revolution.
sentences.zh: 时尚从未如此剧烈、如此迅速地改变过。

sentences.en: Never had before has fashion changed so radically and so quickly.

sentences.zh: 基本上总是盘起来的。

sentences.en: Always up.
sentences.zh: 总是盘起来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And one of the...
sentences.zh: 还有其中一个……

sentences.en: I mean, again, anyone who has particularly watched film,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样，任何看过电影的人，

sentences.en: TV adaptations of Jane Austen, I guess particularly Pride and Prejudice, where Lizzie Bennet is always walking, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 看过简·奥斯汀的电视改编作品，我想特别是《傲慢与偏见》，伊丽莎白·班内特总是在走路，不是吗？

sentences.en: Presumably, it's more difficult for women to ride than it is for men.
sentences.zh: 大概是因为女性骑马比男性更困难。

sentences.en: So in a sense, they're obliged to walk.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，她们被迫走路。

sentences.en: And to what extent does that influence the direction of fashion for women?
sentences.zh: 这在多大程度上影响了女性时尚的方向？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things I really want to explore in the book and to challenge was this idea of kind of women as sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在书中真正想探索和挑战的一点是这种观念，即女性是那种，你知道的，

sentences.en: helpless, languorous beasts kind of stuck on their sofa.
sentences.zh: 无助、慵懒的生物，被困在沙发上。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the joys about that adaptation is that it really showed the physicality of daily life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那部改编作品的乐趣之一就是它真正展示了日常生活的身体力行。

sentences.en: And there's lots of records of Regency women doing 20-mile walks.
sentences.zh: 有很多关于摄政时期女性进行20英里徒步的记录。

sentences.en: And in a sense, the fact that shoes lose their heels for women, they become completely flat.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，女性鞋子失去了鞋跟，变得完全平底，

sentences.en: This really encouraged especially middle-class women to be able to walk more.
sentences.zh: 这确实鼓励了中产阶级女性能够走得更多。

sentences.en: And there's lots of walking shoes with kind of studded soles that give you grip on muddy surfaces.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多带有钉底的步行鞋，可以在泥泞的地面上提供抓地力。

sentences.en: But it's also kind of a matter of economics because a horse was expensive to maintain.
sentences.zh: 但这在某种程度上也是经济问题，因为养马很贵。

sentences.en: And it was often kind of a working thing.
sentences.zh: 而且马通常是用来干活的。

sentences.en: So if there was a horse in the household, it's likely that the men would have to use it for their business.
sentences.zh: 所以如果家里有马，很可能男性必须用它来处理业务。

sentences.en: So walking was very practical.
sentences.zh: 所以走路是非常实际的。

sentences.en: And it's also a way of reinforcing social interactions.
sentences.zh: 这也是加强社交互动的一种方式。

sentences.en: You know, you walk to the village and back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你走到村子里再走回来。

sentences.en: But you also have a whole lot of outer clothing that supports this walking, things like cloaks and palaces and patterns,
sentences.zh: 但你也有很多支持这种步行的外衣，比如斗篷、长袍和套鞋，

sentences.en: which are a kind of a high-raised clog that keep you out of, you know, on unpaved roads, it's dusty in summer, it's muddy in winter.
sentences.zh: 这是一种高底木屐，让你在未铺砌的道路上行走时保持干爽，夏天多尘，冬天泥泞。

sentences.en: So there is lots of clothing that supports this physical activity as well in this period.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个时期，有很多服装也支持这种体力活动。

sentences.en: And you say that of Jane Austen's actual dress, the only known survivals are a pelisse and a shawl and then various items of jewellery.
sentences.zh: 你说简·奥斯汀本人的衣服中，唯一幸存下来的是一件长袍、一条披肩和各种珠宝首饰。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But would Jane Austen have worn high heels?
sentences.zh: 但简·奥斯汀会穿高跟鞋吗？

sentences.en: No, they weren't in fashion.
sentences.zh: 不会，那时不流行。

sentences.en: So people had worn heels 50 years, certainly 100 years earlier, but now they've gone out and they've gone out for women and for men?
sentences.zh: 所以人们在50年前，甚至是100年前穿过高跟鞋，但现在它们已经过时了，而且男女都不穿了？

sentences.en: Except for Nicholas Sarkozy later in life.
sentences.zh: 除了晚年的尼古拉·萨科齐。

sentences.en: So we, on the podcast, we've been very anxious about the fact that the Kaiser, when he went to Cow's yachting, wore the wrong shoes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在播客里一直很担心，德皇去考斯岛游艇度假时穿错了鞋子。

sentences.en: And essentially this was the cause of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 本质上这就是第一次世界大战的起因。

sentences.en: Tom, you also wore the wrong shoes on a yachting holiday.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在游艇度假时也穿错了鞋子。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我确实穿错了。

sentences.en: I mean, be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，老实点。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我确实穿错了。

sentences.en: But I wondered, just on the topic of shoes, could you turn up at a ball at Pemberley and be wearing the wrong shoes?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，就鞋子这个话题，如果你在彭伯利庄园的舞会上穿错了鞋子会怎样？

sentences.en: Would that bring shame on you?
sentences.zh: 那会让你蒙羞吗？

sentences.en: It would, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it's one of those glitches of some historical productions that they've had male characters turn up to balls in boots.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，一些历史剧的漏洞之一就是让男性角色穿着靴子去参加舞会。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I would have definitely worn boots to a ball.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会穿靴子去参加舞会的。

sentences.en: Well, you'd have been flung out then, wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 那你肯定会被赶出来的，不是吗？

sentences.en: You would.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Shame on the name of Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 给桑布鲁克家族丢脸。

sentences.en: But I would have been in full military uniform.
sentences.zh: 但我会穿着全套军装。

sentences.en: People would have welcomed me as a returning hero.
sentences.zh: 人们会欢迎我作为凯旋的英雄。

sentences.en: Oh, that's all right.
sentences.zh: 哦，那没关系。

sentences.en: If it's military uniform, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 如果是军装，那就没问题。

sentences.en: And we'll be coming to that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But just one last thing on what women are wearing.
sentences.zh: 但关于女性穿着的最后一件事。

sentences.en: So I said that, by and large, men are likely to be riding horses than women.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，总的来说，男性比女性更有可能骑马。

sentences.en: But you do say riding habits were Britain's most successful female dress export.
sentences.zh: 但你确实说过骑马装是英国最成功的女性服装出口产品。

sentences.en: So that's good to know.
sentences.zh: 那很高兴知道这一点。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Riding habits were basically the nearest imitation to men's dress that you could get in women's wardrobe.
sentences.zh: 骑马装基本上是女性衣橱里最接近男性服装的模仿品。

sentences.en: And it's quite practical, usually a bodice and a skirt made out of wool, usually tailored like men's clothing and made by tailors who are making for men.
sentences.zh: 而且它相当实用，通常是羊毛做的紧身胸衣和裙子，通常像男装一样剪裁，由为男性制作服装的裁缝制作。

sentences.en: And it was just kind of a hard-wearing practical gown for riding, but also for traveling and sort of casual wear in a sense.
sentences.zh: 它不仅是一种耐穿实用的骑马装，在某种意义上也是旅行和休闲装。

sentences.en: Women are usually riding side style at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时女性通常是侧骑。

sentences.en: So it also has quite voluminous skirts to hide the legs, which shift slightly.
sentences.zh: 所以它也有相当宽大的裙摆来遮盖腿部，裙摆会轻微移动。

sentences.en: And so when, say, 1815, after the Battle of Waterloo, British women go to Paris, do they look completely odd to the French?
sentences.zh: 那么，比如说1815年滑铁卢战役后，英国女性去巴黎时，她们在法国人眼里看起来很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do they look really, they say, yes, you know, anglaise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她们看起来真的很……他们会说，是的，你知道，英式风格。

sentences.en: This is, it's quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: You can trace a definite shift in British fashion from about 1814.
sentences.zh: 你可以追踪到从1814年左右开始，英国时尚发生了明确的转变。

sentences.en: Because, of course, in 1814, we've got the first piece.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，在1814年，我们有了第一件作品。

sentences.en: And there is a kind of tour of European leaders that comes to Britain.
sentences.zh: 当时有一群欧洲领导人来到英国巡访。

sentences.en: So, you know, the Emperor of Russia is there and his sister, the Grand Duchess of Oldenburg, who has a very influential bonnet, the very high-crowned Oldenburg bonnet,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，俄国沙皇在那儿，还有他的妹妹，奥尔登堡大公夫人，她戴着一顶非常有影响力的帽子，那种高冠的奥尔登堡帽，

sentences.en: sweeps Europe.
sentences.zh: 风靡了欧洲。

sentences.en: And that's when you start to sort of get, I mean, there's been interaction between France and Britain for fashion during the whole Napoleonic War period.
sentences.zh: 那就是你开始感觉到的时候，我的意思是，在整个拿破仑战争期间，法国和英国在时尚方面一直有互动。

sentences.en: But that's when you start to get people going, oh, look at what the French are doing.
sentences.zh: 但那是你开始听到人们说，哦，看看法国人在做什么的时候。

sentences.en: And when the English go to Paris, the French think they look slightly dowdy and old-fashioned, and they're too interested in historicalness.
sentences.zh: 当英国人去巴黎时，法国人觉得他们看起来有点邋遢、过时，而且对历史感太感兴趣了。

sentences.en: I know, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道，对吧？

sentences.en: Who'd have thought?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: It's unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 真是不可思议。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 不可思议。

sentences.en: Nobody ever says that about the English.
sentences.zh: 从来没人那样评价英国人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's shocking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: And the French looked, they had still had kind of higher waists, but their skirts were starting to get a bit broader.
sentences.zh: 法国人看起来，他们仍然保持着较高的腰线，但他们的裙子开始变得宽大了一些。

sentences.en: And there's all these slight changes that happen in British fashion between about 1814 and 1815, where it kind of comes more into line with French fashion.
sentences.zh: 在1814年到1815年左右，英国时尚界发生了一些细微的变化，使其与法国时尚更加接轨。

sentences.en: And you start getting people sort of talking about the things they've brought back from Paris,
sentences.zh: 你开始听到人们谈论他们从巴黎带回来的东西，

sentences.en: and also how customs is confiscating some of the things they've brought back from Paris.
sentences.zh: 以及海关如何没收他们从巴黎带回的一些物品。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're not very happy about that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们对此很不高兴。

sentences.en: So hold on, just to recap, Nikolaus von Heidloff, when he said the English were absolute top dogs in the Sartorial arena, are you saying that this view was not, in fact,
sentences.zh: 等等，回顾一下，尼古劳斯·冯·海德洛夫（Nikolaus von Heidloff）说英国人在服装界是绝对的领头羊，你是说这种观点实际上并不是

sentences.en: universally held?
sentences.zh: 普遍持有的吗？

sentences.en: That some people thought the English were a bit boring and fusty and reactionary in their dress?
sentences.zh: 有些人认为英国人在穿着上有点无聊、守旧和保守？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, they did, but it was the French who thought that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们确实这么认为，但那是法国人的看法。

sentences.en: So is that, is that, you know, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以那是，那是，你知道，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, they would, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 是的，他们会这么想，不是吗？

sentences.en: But also, Hilary, I mean, isn't it the case that perhaps female fashion is seen as being less cutting edge, less kind of must-have by people on the continent?
sentences.zh: 但希拉里，我的意思是，女性时尚是否被欧洲大陆的人视为不那么前卫，不那么“必备”？

sentences.en: But male fashion is, I gather from your book, absolutely the bee's knees.
sentences.zh: 但我从你的书中了解到，男性时尚绝对是顶尖的。

sentences.en: Anglomania.
sentences.zh: 安格鲁狂热（Anglomania）。

sentences.en: It is Anglomania, and, you know, it's remarkable how appropriate it becomes.
sentences.zh: 这就是安格鲁狂热，而且，你知道，它变得如此合时宜，真是了不起。

sentences.en: There's quotes saying that, you know, if you are dressed in the English style, you are well-dressed anywhere on the continent for men.
sentences.zh: 有引文说，你知道，如果你穿着英式风格，你在欧洲大陆任何地方都算得上是穿着得体。

sentences.en: I mean, that hasn't changed, has it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点没变，对吧？

sentences.en: That's very true today.
sentences.zh: 今天依然如此。

sentences.en: So what is it about, well, two questions.
sentences.zh: 那么，关于这个问题，嗯，有两个问题。

sentences.en: First of all, what changes about male dress in Britain over the 1790s and the first two decades of the 19th century?
sentences.zh: 首先，在18世纪90年代和19世纪的前二十年里，英国男性的着装发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: And what is it about those changes that strikes people on the continent as so appealing?
sentences.zh: 这些变化中有什么让欧洲大陆的人觉得如此吸引人？

sentences.en: This is kind of a, it's a twofold answer because, like much of the changes, this has also been building during the 1770s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 这是一个双重答案，因为像许多变化一样，这也是在18世纪70年代和80年代逐渐形成的。

sentences.en: And what distinguishes English men's dress from the French is, in a sense, it's casualness.
sentences.zh: 英国男装与法国男装的区别在于，从某种意义上说，是它的随意性。

sentences.en: It's comfort.
sentences.zh: 是舒适感。

sentences.en: The notion of the English country gentleman who is in good, solid leather breeches, he's wearing riding boots,
sentences.zh: 英国乡村绅士的概念，他穿着结实耐用的皮马裤，穿着骑马靴，

sentences.en: and he's got a well-tailored but plain coat that sort of suits him, that he can jump on a horse, he can stride around with the hounds in.
sentences.zh: 穿着一件剪裁得体但朴素的外套，这很适合他，让他可以跳上马，可以带着猎犬四处奔走。

sentences.en: And it's kind of emblematic of more ease and freedom, but also his kind of more democratic abilities as kind of master.
sentences.zh: 这象征着更多的轻松和自由，也象征着他作为主人更民主的能力。

sentences.en: He doesn't have to wear the kind of court, Versailles, and the buckles.
sentences.zh: 他不必穿那种凡尔赛宫廷式的服装和扣子。

sentences.en: Yeah, and all of the embroidery and the silk and the, so it's quite a distinct figure from that.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有所有的刺绣和丝绸，所以这与那种形象截然不同。

sentences.en: So the sort of the country squire has always been held up like that, and the Anglomania really starts to kind of take off in probably the 1780s.
sentences.zh: 所以乡村绅士一直被这样推崇，而安格鲁狂热真正开始流行可能是在18世纪80年代。

sentences.en: So as these kind of new changes come in, it's seen that this style that is there in England, it becomes even more embraced.
sentences.zh: 随着这些新变化的到来，英国的这种风格被认为得到了更广泛的拥护。

sentences.en: And within England, there's an increasing kind of, I suppose, trickle up.
sentences.zh: 在英国国内，我猜有一种逐渐向上的趋势。

sentences.en: You get a lot of men being made fun of for dressing like their grooms or dressing like jockeys, like working men who have kind of practical, comfortable clothing.
sentences.zh: 很多男人因为穿着得像他们的马夫或骑师，像那些穿着实用、舒适服装的劳动者而受到嘲笑。

sentences.en: So it's like Prince Harry or somebody wearing a baseball cap.
sentences.zh: 就像哈里王子或某个人戴着棒球帽一样。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But there's a sort of emphasis on sobriety.
sentences.zh: 但有一种对朴素的强调。

sentences.en: Is that fair that you're, so you're not dressing in a flamboyant way?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？你不是以一种浮夸的方式穿着？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: You're not trying to look like a sort of fop.
sentences.zh: 你不是想看起来像个花花公子。

sentences.en: You're trying to look serious and you wear dark colors.
sentences.zh: 你是想看起来严肃，而且你穿深色衣服。

sentences.en: And that's new, right?
sentences.zh: 那是新的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because previously men had dressed in very, very bold, dramatic, sort of bright colors.
sentences.zh: 因为以前男人们穿得非常、非常大胆、戏剧化，颜色鲜艳。

sentences.en: And in a way, I suppose you could say this is one of those elements of this revolution that has endured.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我想你可以说这是这场革命中延续下来的元素之一。

sentences.en: I mean, men do, by and large, dress much more, much more, less brightly than women, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总的来说，男人的穿着确实比女人少得多，颜色也没那么鲜艳，不是吗？

sentences.en: They absolutely do.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And what we also get from this period, and again, this is still where the English reputation maintains, is good tailoring.
sentences.zh: 我们从这个时期得到的另一个东西，而且这仍然是英国声誉保持的地方，就是精良的剪裁。

sentences.en: Yes, Savile Row.
sentences.zh: 是的，萨维尔街（Savile Row）。

sentences.en: Yes, Savile Row.
sentences.zh: 是的，萨维尔街。

sentences.en: Savile Row's greatness begins during this period because previously the kind of the quality of the fabric and the embroidery and to a sense the decoration was more important.
sentences.zh: 萨维尔街的伟大始于这一时期，因为以前面料的质量、刺绣以及某种程度上的装饰更为重要。

sentences.en: But suddenly you start to get more of an emphasis on kind of quite subdued or austere fabric, but cut beautifully.
sentences.zh: 但突然间，你开始更多地强调相当柔和或朴素的面料，但剪裁非常精美。

sentences.en: So it makes you look better and it enhances the body and it enhances the shoulder.
sentences.zh: 所以它让你看起来更好，增强了身体线条，突出了肩膀。

sentences.en: And you get this new kind of emphasis on this kind of still what is the template male figure of like broad shoulders, strong neck, narrow waist, strong hips,
sentences.zh: 你得到了这种新的强调，即现在仍然是男性身材模板的：宽肩、强壮的脖子、窄腰、强壮的臀部，

sentences.en: which is also coming from classical statues and the classical ideal.
sentences.zh: 这也源于古典雕像和古典理想。

sentences.en: So it's all working in together.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都在共同作用。

sentences.en: But the sense of that the quality of the fabric is not immediately visible, but it's how it's tailored and shaped that's important springs from this period.
sentences.zh: 但那种面料质量不是一眼就能看出来的，重要的是它的剪裁和塑形，这正是源于这一时期。

sentences.en: Well, Hilary, I have a bespoke suit from Savile Row.
sentences.zh: 嗯，希拉里，我有一套萨维尔街的定制西装。

sentences.en: And it does make me look like a Greek dog.
sentences.zh: 它确实让我看起来像个希腊神。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Which one?
sentences.zh: 哪一个？

sentences.en: Hephaestus.
sentences.zh: 赫菲斯托斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, Hephaestus.
sentences.zh: 是的，赫菲斯托斯。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The band.
sentences.zh: 那帮人。

sentences.en: The band.
sentences.zh: 那帮人。

sentences.en: No, it was a friend of mine who was fabulously rich said, I think I can get you a special deal with my tailor.
sentences.zh: 不，是我一个非常有钱的朋友说，我想我可以帮你从我的裁缝那里拿到特别优惠。

sentences.en: I was so excited about it.
sentences.zh: 我当时对此非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And he did get me a special deal, but it was still so expensive.
sentences.zh: 他确实帮我拿到了特别优惠，但还是太贵了。

sentences.en: It was eye-wateringly expensive.
sentences.zh: 贵得让人眼泪直流。

sentences.en: I'm sure, Tom, that will, I'm sure the listeners will love hearing this detail.
sentences.zh: 我相信，汤姆，听众们一定会喜欢听这个细节的。

sentences.en: It makes you really relatable.
sentences.zh: 这让你显得很亲民。

sentences.en: Well, I might, I might, I might, I might, I might post a photo of myself in my Savile Race.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可能会，我可能会，我可能会，我可能会，我可能会发一张我穿着萨维尔街西装的照片。

sentences.en: Oh, that will really endear you to the public.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真的会让你深受公众喜爱。

sentences.en: Yeah, do.
sentences.zh: 是的，发吧。

sentences.en: But still, you, I mean, say, you know, if you're really a Regency gentleman, you say,
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我的意思是，假设，你知道，如果你真的是一位摄政时期的绅士，你会说，

sentences.en: you'd actually be going to different tailors for your coat and for your waistcoat and your trousers.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会去不同的裁缝那里做外套、背心和裤子。

sentences.en: And obviously, obviously, the role model for a well-dressed man about time like myself, as he has always been, is Beau Brummel, who cuts a tremendous dash in your book.
sentences.zh: 显然，显然，像我这样那个时代穿着得体的男人的榜样，一直以来都是博·布鲁梅尔（Beau Brummel），他在你的书中非常出彩。

sentences.en: So, for people who don't know about Beau Brummel, who is basically the model of fine English tailoring and dressing, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些不知道博·布鲁梅尔的人，他基本上是英国精良剪裁和着装的典范，不是吗？

sentences.en: Just, you just tell us about him and how cool he is.
sentences.zh: 你就给我们讲讲他，以及他有多酷。

sentences.en: So, Beau Brummel is very interesting because he was not aristocratic.
sentences.zh: 所以，博·布鲁梅尔非常有趣，因为他不是贵族。

sentences.en: This is a key point about him.
sentences.zh: 这是关于他的一个关键点。

sentences.en: He was a middle-class fellow.
sentences.zh: 他是一个中产阶级的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he still went to Eton, but he was incredibly well-dressed and attentive to clothing himself, but not in a showy way, in a subdued way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他还是去了伊顿公学，但他非常注重穿着，打扮自己，但不是以一种炫耀的方式，而是以一种低调的方式。

sentences.en: So, he was about having the best of things, but not being ostentatious, beautifully laundered shirts, beautifully cut jackets, you know, perfect trousers.
sentences.zh: 所以，他追求的是拥有最好的东西，但不张扬，洗得干干净净的衬衫，剪裁精美的夹克，你知道，完美的裤子。

sentences.en: But his ideal was always that the man in the street should not turn and look at you.
sentences.zh: 但他的理想始终是街上的人不应该转头看你。

sentences.en: You should be so perfectly dressed, you are invisible.
sentences.zh: 你应该穿得如此完美，以至于你隐形了。

sentences.en: And his ideas and way of dressing was kind of like a breath of fresh air.
sentences.zh: 他的理念和着装方式就像一股清新的空气。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I should also say it's very much encapsulating what is already happening in clothing.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，我也应该说，这在很大程度上概括了服装界已经发生的事情。

sentences.en: And he's like the best, he's the apotheosis of what this is.
sentences.zh: 他就像是这一切的巅峰。

sentences.en: And he ended up becoming friends with the Prince Regent and kind of really influencing his clothing and had much more powerful reach about ideas about dress
sentences.zh: 他最终与摄政王成为了朋友，并在很大程度上影响了他的着装，对服装理念产生了更有力的影响，

sentences.en: that weren't necessarily about showiness.
sentences.zh: 这些理念不一定与炫耀有关。

sentences.en: They were about quality and understanding and connoisseurship in clothing that have become incredibly influential.
sentences.zh: 它们关乎服装的质量、理解力和鉴赏力，这些已经变得极具影响力。

sentences.en: And, as I say, he's the figure who best started doing that and wasn't an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我所说，他是最先开始这样做的人，而且他不是贵族。

sentences.en: And so, he's kind of, he looms large over dress history.
sentences.zh: 所以，他在服装史上占据了重要地位。

sentences.en: Well, perhaps through Beau Brummel, we can come to the absolutely key question, which is about trousers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许通过博·布鲁梅尔，我们可以谈谈绝对关键的问题，那就是裤子。

sentences.en: So, Beau Brummel wears trousers.
sentences.zh: 所以，博·布鲁梅尔穿裤子。

sentences.en: You have always wondered about this.
sentences.zh: 你一直对这个问题感到好奇。

sentences.en: Well, I said to you in an earlier podcast, ages ago, that years and years ago, Tom, when I was doing my PhD, I went for a drink with Ted Vallance,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在很久以前的播客里对你说过，很多年前，汤姆，当我在读博士时，我和泰德·瓦伦斯（Ted Vallance）去喝了一杯，

sentences.en: who's been on our podcast to talk about Magna Carta and about the execution of Charles I.
sentences.zh: 他曾上过我们的播客，谈论《大宪章》和查理一世的处决。

sentences.en: And I said to him, Ted, when did people start wearing trousers?
sentences.zh: 我对他说，泰德，人们是从什么时候开始穿裤子的？

sentences.en: And despite the fact that he was doing a PhD at the same time on early modern history, he couldn't give me a definitive date.
sentences.zh: 尽管他当时也在攻读早期现代史的博士学位，但他无法给我一个确切的日期。

sentences.en: Because it's not his period, as he would have known, had he read Hillary's book.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是他的研究时期，如果他读过希拉里的书，他就会知道。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然。

sentences.en: If I'm a man about town in 1770, I'm not wearing trousers.
sentences.zh: 如果我是1770年的城里人，我不会穿裤子。

sentences.en: In 1820, I am wearing trousers.
sentences.zh: 在1820年，我穿着裤子。

sentences.en: So, when's that tipping point?
sentences.zh: 那么，那个转折点是什么时候？

sentences.en: It, again, begins to pick up speed in the 1790s for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 它再次在18世纪90年代开始加速，原因有几个。

sentences.en: So, when we talk about breeches, they are always knee length.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们谈论马裤时，它们总是及膝的。

sentences.en: They finish just underneath the knee.
sentences.zh: 它们刚好在膝盖下方结束。

sentences.en: And the only, this is sort of standard, you know, middle class and upper wear and working wear as well.
sentences.zh: 这是中产阶级、上层阶级以及劳动阶级的标准着装。

sentences.en: And the only people who are wearing lower garments, the only men who are wearing lower garments that run from the waist all the way down to the ankle are sailors.
sentences.zh: 唯一穿着从腰部一直延伸到脚踝的下装的人，唯一穿这种下装的男人是水手。

sentences.en: And they're wearing kind of loose, comfortable trousers on board ship, some working men as well.
sentences.zh: 他们在船上穿着那种宽松、舒适的裤子，一些劳动者也穿。

sentences.en: And this, in a sense, is also what they mean by the sans-culottes in the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这也是法国大革命中“无套裤汉”（sans-culottes）的意思。

sentences.en: They mean they're not wearing breeches, they're wearing trousers.
sentences.zh: 他们的意思是他们不穿马裤，他们穿裤子。

sentences.en: So, in another one of these trickle-up moments, we get a new popularity for ankle-reaching leg wear in the 1790s thanks to war because men in the army are wearing pantaloons,
sentences.zh: 所以，在另一个“逐渐向上”的时刻，由于战争，在18世纪90年代，及踝的腿部服装变得流行起来，因为军队里的男人穿着紧身裤（pantaloons），

sentences.en: which are kind of in between breeches and trousers.
sentences.zh: 这介于马裤和裤子之间。

sentences.en: They're completely tight-fitting to the leg, but they run all the way down.
sentences.zh: 它们完全紧贴腿部，但一直延伸到底部。

sentences.en: So, they're tight like breeches, but they're long like trousers.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们像马裤一样紧，但像裤子一样长。

sentences.en: Hold on, I'm just trying to get my head around pantaloon.
sentences.zh: 等等，我正在努力理解紧身裤（pantaloon）。

sentences.en: A pantaloon is like a legging.
sentences.zh: 紧身裤就像打底裤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, what's Nelson wear?
sentences.zh: 那么纳尔逊穿什么？

sentences.en: Does he wear trousers or pantaloons?
sentences.zh: 他穿裤子还是紧身裤？

sentences.en: He's wearing, for full dress, he's wearing breeches.
sentences.zh: 他穿的是马裤，用于正式场合。

sentences.en: And then I think if he's just hanging around the cabin, he's wearing white dog trousers.
sentences.zh: 然后我想如果他只是在船舱里闲逛，他会穿白色的狗皮裤。

sentences.en: With the lads.
sentences.zh: 和伙计们在一起。

sentences.en: Trousers, okay.
sentences.zh: 裤子，好的。

sentences.en: So, military men and naval men are wearing these ankle-length garments.
sentences.zh: 所以，军人和海军人员穿着这些及踝的服装。

sentences.en: And as the Napoleonic Wars increase and the respect and admiration of the nation increases for these men as well, trousers start to become fashionable.
sentences.zh: 随着拿破仑战争的加剧，国家对这些人的尊重和钦佩也随之增加，裤子开始变得流行起来。

sentences.en: So, again, it's a kind of a casualization because, first of all, pantaloons are easier to get into boots, which you're wearing for riding.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是一种休闲化，因为首先，紧身裤更容易穿进靴子里，而你骑马时需要穿靴子。

sentences.en: So, as riding boots become more popular, pantaloons work with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着骑马靴变得越来越流行，紧身裤与它们搭配得很好。

sentences.en: And they start to creep into fashion.
sentences.zh: 它们开始悄悄进入时尚界。

sentences.en: So, I think it's in 18 – oh, gosh, early on, the Duke of Wellington was actually refused admission to Olmax, the most exclusive social club, because he was wearing trousers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想是在18——哦，天哪，早些时候，威灵顿公爵实际上被拒绝进入最顶级的社交俱乐部奥尔马克（Almack's），因为他穿着裤子。

sentences.en: I think it's about sort of the 1810s.
sentences.zh: 我想那是在1810年代左右。

sentences.en: He wore the wrong trousers.
sentences.zh: 他穿错了裤子。

sentences.en: He wore the wrong trousers.
sentences.zh: 他穿错了裤子。

sentences.en: Wow, history could have been changed there as well.
sentences.zh: 哇，历史在那儿也可能被改写了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Didn't matter how famous you were, it was still not considered acceptable.
sentences.zh: 无论你有多出名，这在当时仍被认为是不合时宜的。

sentences.en: But by about 1820, the use of these trousers, whether tight like pantaloons or just sort of long as trousers that we have now, had just become normalized.
sentences.zh: 但到了1820年左右，这种裤子的使用——无论是像紧身裤那样紧，还是像我们现在穿的这种长裤——已经变得常态化了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is further compounded by the appearance of Russian Cossacks in London in 1814, who are wearing trousers that are pleated at the top and are quite full.
sentences.zh: 1814年俄罗斯哥萨克骑兵出现在伦敦，他们穿着裤管顶部有褶皱且相当宽松的裤子，这进一步加剧了这种趋势。

sentences.en: And imitations of these became popular and were called Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 随后，模仿这种裤子的款式流行了起来，被称为“哥萨克裤”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, I think Lord Liverpool, I think, was the first prime minister to have ever worn trousers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想利物浦伯爵应该是第一位穿长裤的首相。

sentences.en: Because I think there's a famous portrait of Lord Liverpool where he's clearly wearing trousers.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得有一幅利物浦伯爵的著名肖像画，画中他显然穿着长裤。

sentences.en: So, that's my contribution to the old trousers.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对旧式裤子话题的贡献。

sentences.en: Well, my contribution is that the most fashionable, the kind of, maybe the person who makes them really fashionable is Byron, because he has a club foot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的贡献是，最时尚的，或者说让这种裤子真正流行起来的人可能是拜伦，因为他有内翻足。

sentences.en: And so, wearing trousers enables him to disguise his club foot, which I learned from your book.
sentences.zh: 所以，穿长裤让他能够掩盖自己的内翻足，这是我从你的书中了解到的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he definitely finds them more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 没错，他确实觉得穿长裤更舒服。

sentences.en: And also, he spends a lot of time in hotter areas.
sentences.zh: 而且，他花了很多时间在气候更炎热的地区。

sentences.en: They're sort of, they're looser, they're easier.
sentences.zh: 它们比较宽松，穿起来更自在。

sentences.en: But Byron loved trousers because the length meant that he could hide his little foot.
sentences.zh: 但拜伦喜欢长裤是因为裤长意味着他可以遮住那只小脚。

sentences.en: How much he actually popularized them may be sort of, you know, self-anthologizing, because he's not averse to that.
sentences.zh: 他到底在多大程度上推广了这种裤子，可能有点，你知道，自我吹嘘的成分，因为他并不排斥这样做。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you touched on this.
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，你提到了这一点。

sentences.en: The idea that men in red coats, and you, I mean, the Navy as well, you have a picture of a guy called Captain Gilbert Heathcote, who, I mean, sensational.
sentences.zh: 关于穿红外套的男人们，还有你提到的海军，你有一张叫吉尔伯特·希思科特船长的家伙的照片，我的天，太惊艳了。

sentences.en: He's gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 他帅极了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, he's...
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，他……

sentences.en: Yeah, you love this bloke, Tom, don't you?
sentences.zh: 是啊，你很喜欢这家伙，汤姆，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't normally feel homoerotic slurings, but...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我通常不会有那种同性恋倾向的评价，但是……

sentences.en: But you do.
sentences.zh: 但你确实有。

sentences.en: He's quite something...
sentences.zh: 他确实很特别……

sentences.en: He's splendid.
sentences.zh: 他很出色。

sentences.en: He's resplendent.
sentences.zh: 他光彩照人。

sentences.en: So, basically, you say that looking at soldiers is a rare example of Regency women, frankly, appraising the physique of the opposite sex.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上你说的是，观察士兵是摄政时期女性罕见地评价异性体格的例子，坦白说。

sentences.en: And, of course, there's Mrs. Bennett, isn't there, who famously says that there was a time when she liked a red coat.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有贝内特太太，不是吗？她那句名言说她曾经喜欢过红外套。

sentences.en: So, we've talked about how, you know, with Beau Brummel and everything, men's tailoring is becoming sober and respectable.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们已经谈到了博·布鲁梅尔等人是如何让男装变得庄重且体面的。

sentences.en: But, presumably, having all these kind of guys in bright red coats...
sentences.zh: 但是，大概是因为有这么多穿着鲜艳红外套的家伙……

sentences.en: With very tight trousers on.
sentences.zh: 还穿着非常紧的裤子。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Okay, so this was my favourite sentence in your entire book.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是你整本书里我最喜欢的一句话。

sentences.en: Anxieties about male evening dress involved tightness.
sentences.zh: 对男性晚装的焦虑与紧身有关。

sentences.en: So, red coats and tightness.
sentences.zh: 所以，红外套和紧身。

sentences.en: Talk us through that.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这个。

sentences.en: Well, as women's waistline rose on dresses, the fronts of men's waistcoats were also rising.
sentences.zh: 嗯，随着女性裙装腰线的升高，男性马甲的前襟也在升高。

sentences.en: So, where in the 1770s or 80s they largely covered the groin, by the sort of about 1800, you suddenly had the entire area from the waist right down to the ankle visible.
sentences.zh: 所以，在18世纪70或80年代，它们基本上遮住了腹股沟，而到了1800年左右，你突然发现从腰部一直到脚踝的整个区域都露出来了。

sentences.en: And so, in men's dress, you also have coats that are cut away at the origin of our modern tailcoats where they're slightly higher front and, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，在男装中，你也看到了现代燕尾服雏形的剪裁，它们的前襟稍微高了一些，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: nothing to cover at the front.
sentences.zh: 前面没有什么遮挡物。

sentences.en: So, there's a lot more of the male loins, shall we say, on display and in focus than there has previously been.
sentences.zh: 所以，可以说，男性下体展示和聚焦的程度比以前要多得多。

sentences.en: And when you combine that with, you know, the appeal of the uniform on top, whether that's red for the army or kind of blue for the navy, there's a lot to look at.
sentences.zh: 当你把这一点与制服的吸引力结合起来时，无论是陆军的红色还是海军的蓝色，确实有很多看点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, would it be fair to say that, I mean, just elaborate what we touched on at the start of this section, that what happens with male dress,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果说——我们详细阐述一下本节开头提到的内容——男装发生的变化，

sentences.en: there is a continuity from this period that is still with us to this day.
sentences.zh: 从那个时期开始有一种延续性，一直保留到今天，这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: So, whether it's men wearing very tight jeans, whether it's a suit that has become a kind of global uniform, the origin point for those kind of trends are this period in Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是男人穿紧身牛仔裤，还是西装成为一种全球通用的制服，这些潮流的起源点都是英国的这一时期。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And the way that men's dress transforms in the 1790s and 1800s sets the template for essentially Western men's dress that is still with us today.
sentences.zh: 18世纪90年代和19世纪初男装的转型，为今天依然存在的西方男装奠定了模板。

sentences.en: But can I ask about two things that are not with us today?
sentences.zh: 但我能问两件今天已经不存在的事情吗？

sentences.en: One of them is wigs.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是假发。

sentences.en: So, at what point do people drop wigs?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们是在什么时候放弃假发的？

sentences.en: Well, one of the interesting things I came across in my research is that it actually takes a while for people to drop wigs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在研究中发现的一个有趣的事情是，人们放弃假发其实花了一段时间。

sentences.en: They're just not so obvious.
sentences.zh: 它们只是没那么显眼了。

sentences.en: So, the kind of the white powdered wig that is so emblematic of the 18th century, people still wear wigs, they just do it with natural coloured hair.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种18世纪标志性的白色扑粉假发，人们仍然戴假发，只是改用了自然色的头发。

sentences.en: So, you know, you're wearing a wig, but it's, you know, brown and it's sort of…
